note: The first tranche: the surah every Muslim recites seventeen times a day, the verse the Prophet called the greatest in the Book, the three verses ash-Shafi'i said would have sufficed a people, and the four that weigh a third of the Qur'an. They are here first because they are said most, and because a small complete thing proves the shape better than a large unfinished one.

1.sense: The Book does not open by announcing itself. It opens by naming the One it comes from, and the two names it chooses out of all the names are both names of mercy. Everything that follows, including the warnings, is being said by the One who introduced Himself this way.

notes.t: Whether this line is the first verse of Al-Fatiha, or a line of separation that stands before it, is an old and settled difference. The reading of Hafs, which this Mushaf follows, counts it as verse one; the Maliki and Hanafi schools do not count it as a verse of the surah. Nobody disputes that the words are the Qur'an's.
notes.src: a difference between the schools and the readings, not between authentic and weak

notes.t: The Prophet ﷺ opened his letter to Heraclius with these words before anything else, which is why they are the ordinary Muslim opening of a letter, a meal and a road.
notes.src: Bukhari 7

notes.t: Rahman and Rahim grow from one root, r-h-m, the root of the womb. Most exegetes read Rahman as the mercy that covers everything alive right now, believer and denier alike, and Rahim as the mercy He keeps in reserve for those who turn to Him. The distinction is a reading, not a text.

links.why: Sulayman's letter to the queen of Sheba begins with the same line
Nuh launches the ark in the name of Allah

2.sense: Not I praise Allah, which would make the praise a thing I produce, but praise belongs to Allah, which is a statement about where praise already lives whether or not anyone says it. The first thing the Book teaches you to say about your Lord is that He deserves this before you arrived.

notes.t: The Prophet ﷺ reported that Allah said: I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant in two halves, and My servant shall have what he asks. When the servant says al-hamdu lillahi rabbil-alamin, Allah says: My servant has praised Me. Every verse of this surah has an answer, and this is the first.
notes.src: Muslim 395

notes.t: Rabb is weaker in English than in Arabic. An owner owns; a rabb raises a thing stage by stage until it reaches what it was for. The word carries feeding, guarding and finishing, not only possession.
The plural, the worlds, is left open. The Qur'an never fixes their number, and the exegetes who tried disagreed with each other.
notes.src: at-Tabari records several counts and settles on none

links.why: one of five surahs that open on this same word of praise
praise placed at the head of creation

3.sense: The two names return one verse after they were first said. Nothing else in the surah is repeated. They sit between Lord of the worlds and Master of the Day of Judgement, which places mercy between the power that made you and the reckoning that awaits you.

notes.t: The same report continues: when the servant says ar-Rahman ar-Rahim, Allah says: My servant has extolled Me.
notes.src: Muslim 395

notes.t: Saying a thing twice in Arabic is not padding, it is emphasis, and the placement here does the argument. A reader who has just heard Lord of all the worlds might brace for the Day that follows. The verse in between tells him what kind of Master that will be.

links.why: My mercy encompasses all things
He has decreed mercy upon Himself

4.sense: Ownership of that Day belongs to one Being alone. On every other day authority is shared out among people who can be argued with, bought, or outlived. On that one it is not shared at all.

notes.t: Two authentic readings stand here, and both are recited to this day: Maaliki, Owner of the Day, and Maliki, King of the Day. Hafs from Asim, the reading in this Mushaf, has Maaliki. Neither reading is a variant in the sense of an error; both were transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ.
notes.src: the ten canonical readings; Hafs reads Māliki, Nafiʿ and Ibn Kathir read Maliki

notes.t: The report continues: when the servant says Maliki yawmi-d-din, Allah says: My servant has glorified Me.
notes.src: Muslim 395

notes.t: Din here is not religion, though it is the same three letters. It is recompense, what comes back to you. The related word dayn means a debt, and the image underneath is of an account being settled exactly.

links.why: the Day when no soul holds any power for another
sovereignty given and taken away

5.sense: The hinge of the surah. Everything before it was said about Allah; from here on it is said to Him. And it is said in the plural, we, by a person who may be entirely alone on a prayer mat at three in the morning.

notes.t: In Arabic the object normally follows the verb. Here it is pulled in front of it, twice, and that inversion is how the language says only. Not we worship You, but You, and no other, we worship.
The report names this verse as the join: this verse is between Me and My servant in two halves, and My servant shall have what he asked for.
notes.src: Muslim 395

notes.t: Worship comes before asking for help, and the exegetes read the order as deliberate: you establish who He is before you tell Him what you need. The reading is theirs, and the order is the text's.

links.why: so worship Him and rely upon Him
take Him as a disposer of affairs

6.sense: The only request in the surah, and it is made by people who are already praying. Guidance here is not a door you walk through once. It is asked for again in the next prayer, by the same person, because it is being asked for the next few hours and not for the rest of a life.

notes.t: The report gives the answer to this half: these are for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asked for.
notes.src: Muslim 395

notes.t: Sirat is not a narrow track. The lexicographers describe it as a wide, clear, public road, the kind a whole people can walk down at once. The narrowness people imagine is imported.
Straight, mustaqim, is the participle of a verb that means to stand upright and stay standing. A straight road in Arabic is one that holds its direction, not merely one without bends.

links.why: this is My path, straight, so follow it
the Prophet ﷺ himself is told he guides to a straight path, and told whose path it is

7.sense: The straight road is defined by the people already on it rather than by a rule, and then by two ways of leaving it. The verse does not say which two peoples; it says two conditions, and it asks to be kept out of both.

notes.t: The Qur'an answers its own question about who was favoured: the prophets, the truthful, the witnesses and the righteous, and it names them in another place.

A well-known report from Adi ibn Hatim identifies the two groups as the Jews and the Christians. Its grading is discussed and many exegetes accept it. Many of those same exegetes, at-Tabari and Ibn Kathir among them, read the two as descriptions of two failures rather than sentences on two peoples: knowing the truth and not acting on it, and acting hard without knowledge. On that reading the danger belongs to the person praying, which is why he is asking to be spared it.
notes.src: Tirmidhi 2953, graded hasan; the reading of it differs among the exegetes

notes.t: The one thing the Prophet ﷺ attached to the end of this verse is a word: when the imam finishes wa lad-dallin, say Ameen.
notes.src: Bukhari 780

links.why: the four kinds of people the favour landed on
the request this verse is completing

255.sense: Ayat al-Kursi is one sentence of theology said without a single pause for objection. It denies Allah a partner, then sleep, then any intercessor who has not been permitted, then any limit on His knowledge, then any strain in holding all of it. Each clause closes a door that human beings habitually leave open when they imagine God.

notes.t: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Kaʿb which verse of the Book of Allah was the greatest. Ubayy answered with this one, and the Prophet ﷺ struck him on the chest and said: may knowledge be pleasant for you, Abu al-Mundhir.
notes.src: Muslim 810

notes.t: Abu Hurayra was told by a thief he caught at night: when you go to your bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi, and a guardian from Allah will remain over you and no devil will come near you until morning. The Prophet ﷺ confirmed it, and added that the thief had been Satan, and had told the truth while being a habitual liar.
notes.src: Bukhari 2311

notes.t: Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him is not a small remark. Sleep is the daily proof that a living thing is not self-sufficient. Denying it denies the whole category of need.

What the Kursi is has more than one answer from the earliest generations. Reports from Ibn Abbas describe it as the place of the two Feet, distinct from the Throne; another report from him reads it as His knowledge. The scholars did not agree, and the honest position is that the word is affirmed and its manner is not known.
notes.src: reports from Ibn ʿAbbās point both ways; at-Tabari lists them without deciding

notes.t: They encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. The verse concedes that human beings do know things, and then names the only reason they do.

links.why: the verse immediately after, on compulsion in religion, is read by many as its consequence
the same two names, al-Hayy al-Qayyum, open Aal Imran
faces humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer

1.sense: The surah opens with an oath, and Allah swears by time itself. Whatever else time is, it is the one asset every human being is spending at exactly the same rate and cannot add to.

notes.t: What al-asr means here is not agreed. The age, time in general, the late afternoon and its prayer, and the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ have all been held by serious exegetes. The oath works under every one of them.
notes.src: at-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record the several positions without settling one

notes.t: An oath in the Qur'an is not there to convince a doubter that Allah is telling the truth. It points at the thing sworn by and tells you to look at it, and here the thing is the hour you are currently inside.

links.why: another surah opening on oaths by pieces of time

2.sense: The verdict is given on the whole species and given first, before any exception. Not that man may lose, but that he is in loss, present tense, as a standing condition.

notes.t: Khusr is a merchant's word. It is what you say about a deal that came back with less than went into it. The verse frames a life as a transaction that is currently running at a deficit.
The word is left indefinite, khusrin rather than al-khusr, which in Arabic makes it vast and unspecified rather than a particular known loss.

links.why: the scales, and who is found light

3.sense: Four things pull a life out of deficit, and two of them cannot be done alone. Belief and deeds are between a person and his Lord. Counselling to truth and counselling to patience require somebody else in the room.

notes.t: Tawasaw is a reciprocal form: each counsels the other and is counselled in turn. It rules out a version of this that is only ever given and never received.

Two of the Prophet ﷺ's ﷺ companions, when they met, would not part until one of them had recited this surah to the other. The report is in at-Tabarani and has been graded authentic by some and questioned by others.
notes.src: at-Tabarani; graded sahih by al-Albani, contested by others

notes.t: Ash-Shafiʿi is quoted saying that if people reflected on this surah alone it would be enough for them. It is a scholar's remark, not a hadith, and it is worth what a scholar's remark is worth.
notes.src: quoted by Ibn Kathir in his commentary on the surah

links.why: the same pairing of faith with mutual counsel to patience and mercy
cooperate in righteousness and piety

1.sense: An instruction and then an answer. Someone had asked what this God is, expecting a description in the terms they already used for gods, and the reply refuses the terms rather than filling them in.

notes.t: Ahad is not the ordinary counting one, which is wahid. Wahid is one of a possible series; ahad is oneness that admits no second at all, which is why the word is almost never used of created things in the affirmative.
The occasion reported is that the idolaters, and in another narration a group of Jews, said: describe your Lord to us, and this was revealed. The narrations differ and their grading is discussed.
notes.src: Tirmidhi 3364 and others; the chains and gradings are disputed

notes.t: The surah begins with Say, which keeps it audibly a message being handed over rather than a statement the speaker thought of.

links.why: your God is one God
do not take two gods; He is only one God

2.sense: One word, and it is the hardest word in the surah to carry into English. Every translation of it is a choice among meanings the Arabic holds at once.

notes.t: The early generations gave several readings of as-Samad: the one every creature turns to in need and who needs nobody; the one who is solid all the way through, with no hollow, who does not eat or drink; the one complete in every attribute. These are not rival guesses so much as facets, and the exegetes preserved all of them.
notes.src: reports from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Hasan and others, collected by at-Tabari

notes.t: The verse repeats the name Allah instead of saying He, which in Arabic re-anchors the sentence and makes the second statement stand on its own rather than lean on the first.

links.why: you are the ones in need of Allah, and He is the Free of need

3.sense: Two denials, and between them they cut every family line a people has ever attached to a god: no offspring below, no origin above. Birth is how created things enter and continue, and He is outside it in both directions.

notes.t: The Qur'an makes the same denial elsewhere and argues it: how could He have a son when He has no companion, and He created all things.

The order matters. Did not beget comes first, answering the claims made in the Prophet ﷺ's own city and beyond it; was not begotten follows, closing the question of where He came from before it can be asked.

links.why: the heavens almost rupture at the claim that the Most Merciful took a son
the argument stated directly

4.sense: The last door. Having denied Him a partner, a need and a lineage, the surah denies Him a peer of any kind, and closes on the same word it opened with.

notes.t: The Prophet ﷺ said of this surah that it is equal to a third of the Qur'an. The scholars explain the share as its subject rather than its reward: the Qur'an teaches creed, law and story, and this surah is creed in four verses.
notes.src: Bukhari 5013

notes.t: Kufu is the word used for a marriage match, someone of comparable standing. Its use here denies not only rivalry but comparability.
Ahad opens verse one and closes verse four, so the surah is a ring. Whatever you were told in between, you are put back where you started.

links.why: there is nothing like unto Him
do you know of any namesake for Him
